statements.t: Based on our year-to-date results and the optionality of our model, we are raising our full year earnings outlook.”
The ASR will be completed under the Company’s existing $750 million share repurchase authorization.
Upon completion of the planned share repurchases in the fourth quarter, the Company expects to have approximately $230 million remaining under its existing share repurchase authorization.
The Company’s outlook assumes a 12.5 percent reciprocal tariff rate in the fourth quarter based on currently available information.
On an adjusted basis, the Company has excluded the impact of the 2025-related IEEPA tariffs and associated refunds in its 2026 outlook.

"We are updating our full year outlook to reflect our year-to-date results, the successful completion and final terms of the divestiture of Lee, as well as stronger gross margin expansion and earnings growth,” said Joe Alkire, President and Chief Financial Officer.

We expect to deliver another year of strong results in 2027 and have visibility to adjusted EPS of at least $6.60, reflecting more than 20 percent growth, and more than $325 million of cash flow from operations.
Beyond 2027, we expect our cash flow from operations to exceed $400 million."

The Company’s updated outlook reflects the final terms of the divestiture of Lee which has resulted in changes to the classification of certain income, expense and cash flow items relative to the prior outlook as detailed below.
The Company’s full year 2026 outlook also includes the following assumptions:

Incremental expenses previously allocated to Lee will be predominantly offset by fees expected to be received for services the Company will provide in support of the transition of the Lee business, which will be classified as other income.
• The Company now expects an effective tax rate of approximately 18.5 percent on adjusted pre-tax earnings, reflecting additional tax synergies from the Helly Hansen integration.
Other income now reflects fees expected to be received for services the Company will provide in support of the transition of the Lee business.
• The Company now expects total cash from operations to approximate $325 million.
The Company's updated outlook also includes additional inventory investments in Wrangler and Helly Hansen to support future growth and service levels as a result of current supply chain volatility.
• The Company now expects to make voluntary term loan payments of $280 million in the fourth quarter and achieve a net leverage ratio below 1.5 times by year-end.
The Company continues to expect the divestiture of Lee to be immaterial to earnings per share over a 12-to-18-month period.

The earnings contribution of the Lee business is anticipated to be offset through capital deployment of the net proceeds from the divestiture, and mitigation of overhead and other expenses previously allocated to Lee, through fees received for services the Company will provide in support of the transition of the Lee business, restructuring and other mitigating cost actions.

The Company's initial 2027 cash from operations outlook includes elevated one-time costs to support the Helly Hansen systems migration and anticipated restructuring and other costs required to fully offset the expenses previously allocated to the Lee business.

The Company has responded to ongoing macroeconomic conditions by controlling expenses, instituting pricing adjustments for our products, investing in our brands and executing our Project Jeanius business transformation.

While we anticipate continued uncertainty related to the macroeconomic environment during the remainder of 2026, including the potential impact of further tariff rate changes, we believe we are appropriately positioned to successfully manage through operational challenges and cost pressures should they arise.
We expect to incur additional costs in future periods primarily related to the information technology integration of Helly Hansen.
The Company expects the reorganized legal entity structure to align legal ownership with the operating model and facilitate future integration synergies and a simplified operating structure.
The Company completed its execution of Project Jeanius during the third quarter of 2026.
We expect to incur additional costs related to our ongoing transformation in future periods.

Operating margin increased to 25.3%, compared to 24.7% for the 2025 period, due to the benefits of Project Jeanius and favorable business mix and pricing, net of changes in product costs, partially offset by other operating cost increases driven by higher investments in demand creation, technology and our direct-to-consumer businesses.

Operating margin increased to 27.6%, compared to 23.0% for the 2025 period, driven by the benefits of Project Jeanius, the U.S. tariff receivable recorded in the first quarter of 2026 and favorable business and pricing, net of changes in product costs, partially offset by other operating cost increases driven by higher investments in demand creation, technology and our direct-to-consumer business.

We believe cash flows from operations will support our short-term liquidity needs as well as any future liquidity and capital requirements, in combination with available cash balances and borrowing capacity from our revolving credit facility.

As of September 2026, the Company was in compliance with all applicable covenants under the 2025 Credit Agreement and expects to maintain compliance with the applicable covenants for at least one year from the issuance of these financial statements.
The Company intends to continue to pay cash dividends in future periods.

The Company intends to utilize the proceeds from the sale for share repurchases and debt repayments.

On November 5, 2026, the Company announced it anticipates entering into accelerated share repurchase agreements (the "ASR Agreements") with multiple financial institutions to repurchase an aggregate of $400 million of the Company's shares of Common Stock as part of its 2026 Repurchase Program, commencing in the fourth quarter of 2026.
The Company expects the final settlement of the transactions under the ASR Agreements to occur during the first half of 2027.

We anticipate that we will have sufficient cash flows from operations, along with existing borrowing capacity, to support continued investments in our brands, infrastructure, talent and capabilities, dividend payments to shareholders, repayment of our debt obligations when due and repurchases of Common Stock.

We currently expect capital expenditures to be approximately $25.0 million in 2026, primarily to support technology, distribution, manufacturing, owned retail store investments and facility improvements.
